clue.text: Argentine machine operators, maybe

parts.note: Argentine here is not the South American nationality but the old adjective for silvery (Latin argentum), and the things that set slot machines going are coins

explanation.surface: Workers from Argentina who run machinery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Argentine' pulls towards Argentina; it is the poetic word for silvery, and a slot machine is operated by putting money in.
explanation.definitionFit: Pieces of silver currency are what you feed into vending machines, the operators of such devices.

clue.text: Insisted upon union?

parts.note: a wedding forced on a couple, traditionally by a bride's father with a firearm, is a union that someone insisted upon

explanation.surface: Someone demanding that workers join a trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union' suggests trade unions, but here it is a wedding forced through, proverbially at gunpoint, often because of a pregnancy.
explanation.definitionFit: A hasty wedding compelled by family pressure is a union imposed on the couple rather than freely chosen.

clue.text: A gamble many take to

parts.note: a lot means a great many

explanation.surface: Lots of people enjoy a flutter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take' is just a link joining the two pieces; the surface suggests a game many people take to.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a lottery-style game of chance, so playing it is a bet on numbers.

clue.text: Note never wrong when this smooth course is maintained

indicators.note: the letters of these two words are put wrong, that is set out in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A musician who keeps steady never hits a wrong note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges NOTE NEVER; the phrase means a calm, unbroken course, as in 'the even tenor of his life'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a steady, untroubled progress of life or affairs, an untroubled course.

clue.text: High speed piece of film

definitions.meaning: a fast ... means a high rate of going
a short extract from a movie or video is a ...

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a brisk pace is a good rate, and a short excerpt is cut from footage.

clue.text: What the captain and his crew talk over

definitions.text: What the captain and his crew talk over

parts.words: What the captain and his crew talk over
parts.note: talk over suggests discussing, but here it means the device through which an aircraft captain speaks to the cabin staff

explanation.surface: A ship's skipper and crew discussing their plans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'talk over' reads as 'discuss'; it is literally the system they talk over, the internal telephone of an aircraft or ship.
explanation.definitionFit: An internal two-way speaker system lets a pilot address the cabin staff on board.

clue.text: Bags of coal fires

definitions.meaning: coal is delivered in large bags called ...
to fire a worker is to dismiss them, also called giving them the sack

explanation.definitionFit: Coal comes in large bags, and an employer who dismisses staff gives them the sack.

clue.text: Sailors about to procure equipment for shooting practice

indicators.note: the sailors' word stands about, around, the second piece

parts.note: tars is an old word for sailors
to procure is to get

explanation.surface: Seamen buy gear to practise their shooting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts TARS round GET.
explanation.definitionFit: Archers and marksmen practise on boards or figures they aim at, the gear of a shooting range.

clue.text: The spirited character of a nicer sort of ship?

indicators.note: a sort of the letters means they are sorted into a new order

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: Asking what gives a better kind of ship its spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges A NICER into RACINE, then SS (steamship) follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Raciness is liveliness or spirited verve, a zesty quality in style or character.

clue.text: Hotel isn't classified? Oh, but it is!

indicators.note: classified means sorted, so the letters of these words are sorted into a new order

explanation.surface: A hotel denied an official rating protests that it does have one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'classified' rearranges HOTEL ISN'T; the retort 'Oh, but it is!' insists the hotel is listed after all, which is what the answer says.
explanation.definitionFit: Being included in an official register is the protest that the hotel does have its rating.

clue.text: I fish out something to sit on

indicators.note: the fish's word is laid out around, on the outside of, the single letter

parts.note: the char is a fish of the trout family

explanation.surface: An angler pulls a catch from the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fish out' looks like 'catch'; 'out' puts CHAR outside I.
explanation.definitionFit: A seat with a back for one person is a piece of furniture for sitting.

clue.text: 1 across? Fourpenny ones

definitions.meaning: the cross-reference points to the solution of the first across clue, silver money; the old English groat was a silver piece
the groat was worth four old pence; a fourpenny one is also slang for a punch

explanation.definitionFit: The medieval groat was a silver piece valued at four old pence.

clue.text: Get Piers inordinately good reputation

indicators.note: inordinately means out of order, so these letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: Piers is urged to build an excessive good name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inordinately' rearranges GET PIERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Prestige is high standing earned in others' eyes, a widely admired name.

clue.text: She's a big noise in Tyne and Wear

indicators.note: the first pieces go in the abbreviation for the region

parts.note: Tyne and Wear is in north-east England, abbreviated NE
a din is a loud noise

explanation.surface: A loud woman is famous on Tyneside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts A and DIN inside NE. 'Big noise' suggests a celebrity, but it is a din. Tyne and Wear is a county around Newcastle in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's first name can stand for 'she', a female person.

clue.text: Confusion that results when Pluto takes command

parts.note: Dis is another name for Pluto, Roman god of the underworld
an order is a command

explanation.surface: Chaos when the god of the underworld assumes control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' just joins the pieces; Pluto is the underworld god, not the dwarf planet.
explanation.definitionFit: Disorder is a state of muddle or chaos, a lack of proper arrangement.

clue.text: Snobs by trade? Nonsense!

definitions.meaning: snob is an old dialect word for a shoemaker or shoe-mender

explanation.definitionFit: Shoe-menders were once called snobs, and the British slang word is an exclamation meaning rubbish.

clue.text: The makings of a skeleton service, perhaps?

definitions.text: The makings of a skeleton service, perhaps?

parts.words: The makings of a skeleton service, perhaps?
parts.note: a skeleton service suggests a minimal staff, but here a dinner service made from material containing skeletal ash

explanation.surface: What it takes to run a minimum-staffing arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skeleton service' means a reduced service; read literally, it is a set of tableware made with bone ash.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine porcelain made with powdered animal bones is what a tea or dinner set may be made of.

clue.text: See 1
Defective hearing that can lead to serious injustice

definitions.text: Defective hearing that can lead to serious injustice

parts.words: Defective hearing that can lead to serious injustice
parts.note: defective hearing suggests deafness, but it is a court hearing invalidated by error

explanation.surface: Poor hearing that causes a grave miscarriage of justice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hearing' tempts towards ears; it is a trial in court, and one conducted with a fatal flaw.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal proceeding declared void through error is a flawed court case.

clue.text: An Indian health official I can get on to

parts.note: MOH is the Medical Officer of Health

explanation.surface: Getting along with a native American public health officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get on to' just links; MOH is the Medical Officer of Health, a British local health post.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mohicans are a Native American people, so one member is a North American Indian.

clue.text: A newcomer to mint?

parts.note: a newcomer to the mint suggests a novice coin-maker, but it is something in mint, never-handled, condition

explanation.surface: A trainee newly joined at the Royal Mint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mint' suggests the coin factory; 'in mint condition' means brand new and never used.
explanation.definitionFit: Something never yet put to use is as good as new, fresh and untouched.

clue.text: Clearly not a nudist who works behind the scenes

definitions.meaning: in theatre, the person who helps actors into costume backstage

explanation.definitionFit: One who puts on clothes is no naturist, and a theatre assistant helps actors with costumes backstage.

clue.text: They are prepared to take obstacles in their stride

definitions.text: They are prepared to take obstacles in their stride

parts.words: They are prepared to take obstacles in their stride
parts.note: taking obstacles in your stride sounds like coping calmly with trouble, but here it describes athletes clearing barriers on a track

explanation.surface: Resilient people who cope with any difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for coping calmly is read literally: track athletes who jump barriers mid-stride.
explanation.definitionFit: Athletes in barrier races leap fences without breaking their running step.

clue.text: Goes over a medieval scene of combat

definitions.meaning: to list a series is to go over it, itemising each one
the ... were the enclosed ground for jousting tournaments

explanation.definitionFit: Itemising things one by one runs through them, and jousting knights fought in an enclosed tilting ground.

clue.text: Not often found in short supply

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are rare: seldom met with, and too little available to meet demand.

clue.text: A sovereign state?

parts.note: a sovereign state suggests an independent nation, but here it is the domain a monarch rules over

explanation.surface: An independent nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sovereign state' means an independent country; read as 'a sovereign's state', it is a kingdom.
explanation.definitionFit: A kingdom is the territory ruled by a king or queen.

clue.text: Sly look one might get from a day-old chick

definitions.text: one might get from a day-old chick
definitions.meaning: the tiny chirp of a young bird

explanation.definitionFit: A furtive glance is a quick look, and a newly hatched chick makes a small high chirp.

clue.text: A board meeting will decide its outcome

definitions.text: A board meeting will decide its outcome

parts.words: A board meeting will decide its outcome
parts.note: a board meeting suggests company directors, but here it is the pieces meeting on a chequered board

explanation.surface: Company directors gathering to settle a result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'board meeting' suggests a boardroom; it is the encounter of pieces on a board in a game of kings and pawns.
explanation.definitionFit: A game for two played with pieces on a sixty-four square board is settled across that board.

clue.text: New World amalgam of main races?

definitions.note: the def names a place; the answer is its people, the Western Hemisphere's inhabitants

indicators.note: an amalgam is a mixture, so the letters are mixed together

explanation.surface: The New World as a melting pot of the main races.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amalgam of' rearranges MAIN RACES; the surface's melting pot fits the US.
explanation.definitionFit: The Western Hemisphere was called the New World, and its people, especially of the United States, are named for that continent.

clue.text: Timid stockholder with wide ranging interests

definitions.text: Timid stockholder with wide ranging interests

parts.words: Timid stockholder with wide ranging interests
parts.note: a timid stockholder suggests a cautious investor, but here the stock is livestock of timid woolly animals kept on open ranges

explanation.surface: A nervous investor with diverse holdings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stockholder' and 'interests' suggest finance; the stock is livestock, timid flock animals, grazing wide ranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A rancher who raises woolly flocks keeps livestock across open grazing land.
